newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Informer blames ex-cop for Argentine newsman murder.
newsitem.headline: Informer blames ex-cop for Argentine newsman murder.

text.p: A 28-year-old man who was involved in the murder of an Argentine news photographer has turned informer and identified an ex-policeman suspected of pulling the trigger, officials said on Friday.

"It is too soon to talk about the case being solved, but I am convinced we now have firm evidence," said Eduardo Duhalde, governor of Buenos Aires Province, where the charred body of Noticias news magazine photographer Jose Luis Cabezas was found in a car near an Atlantic beach resort in January.
The 35-year-old newsman was handcuffed, beaten, shot in the head, doused with fuel and burned to a blackened skeleton.

The murder horrified Argentina, reviving dark memories of the "death squads" of the 1970s, and has led to widespread outcry and street protests. Cabezas' picture has been posted on walls everywhere, and some television stations have taken to ending their newscasts with the words: "Don't Forget Cabezas."
The informer was among four people, including two police officers, arrested on Wednesday on the orders of Judge Jose Luis Macchi. Another ex-policeman was arrested on Friday.
In his eight-hour confession on Thursday, the informer told Macchi how an ex-policeman paid him and four others to "scare" the Noticias newsman, and how the plan went horribly wrong.

Macchi's secretary Mariano Cazeaux told reporters the confession of Hector Miguel Retana "gave us some truly amazing details." But the press lobbying group ADEPA advised "plenty of caution," and Cabezas' close colleague Gabriel Micchi said: "It's very premature to say the case is closed."

The media identified the man who hired Retana as Gustavo Prellezo, a former inspector for the Buenos Aires Province Police and one of the four suspects arrested. The Clarin newspaper said Retana was not present when Cabezas was killed, but was told by Prellezo later: "It all went wrong. We had to kill him because he recognised one of us."

Retana said he was hired "to beat up a photographer" who was investigating a crime wave on the coast run by corrupt officers of the Buenos Aires force, which has a terrible reputation for corruption and brutality.

Gov. Duhalde, a presidential hopeful who is purging his police force, said it remained to be seen whether "the people who killed Cabezas are the ones who ordered his murder." A gang of five led by Margarita Di Tulio, alias "Pepita la Pistolera" (Pepita the Gunslinger) have been held in connection with the crime since February.
Cabezas' wife Maria Cristina, speaking to local media 76 days after the killing, said: "I can wait six months more, but I don't want just anybody blamed, I want the real culprits."
